why: Source: locate Country 4 row, daily profit, annualise, divide cost by annual profit, round up to the first option past break-even (5 steps); question: the same five steps with different numbers (5 steps).

Source: profit per cup, divide by cup size to get per litre, scale by 1,000 to per thousand litres, discard unused cu (4 steps); question: profit per bottle, divide by size to get per millilitre, convert to per litre with 1,000, discard unused b (4 steps).

Source: read unlabelled margin lines, profit for the lead category, profit for the other three, compare, then check three revenue-share, growth and margin-decline statements (about 7 steps); question: the same readings, products and four statement checks on the same table-plus-unlabelled-line layout (about 7 steps).
Source: pick the indirect segments from a labelled stacked bar (avoiding totals), sum them, apply the percentage to 2013 GDP (3 steps); question: the same pick, sum and percentage (3 steps).

Source: read bar-note profits and margins, derive total sales per year, divide segment profit by sales, compare across years (4 steps); question: the same derivation, division and comparison (4 steps).

Source: read bar-note profits and margins, derive total sales per year, divide segment profit by sales, compare across years (4 steps); question: the same derivation, division and comparison (4 steps).

Source: two losses from revenue times negative margin and compare, sum revenue, costs as revenue times (1 + |margin|) for two statements (about 5 steps); question: the same loss comparison, revenue sum and two cost checks (about 5 steps).

Source: usage per unit for both firms and compare, plus three no-calculation statements rejected as unsupported (3 steps); question: diesel per van for both firms and compare, plus three unsupported statements rejected (3 steps).

Source: ten-year growth multiples for two rows and extrapolate to 20 years, past growth versus rest of market, annualised growth comparison, share four years ago (about 6 steps); question: the same four statement checks with the same calculations (about 6 steps).
Source: divide income by exchange rate to get dollars, then multiply by PPP rate (2 steps); question: divide distance by fuel economy to get litres, then multiply by price per litre (2 steps).
